title: Incremental Causal Graph Learning for Online Root Cause Analysis

problem.claim: Root cause analysis identifies the root causes of system faults or failures using system monitoring data.

gap.claim: Previous research has mostly focused on offline RCA algorithms that may require manual initiation, substantial time and data for robust model training, and retraining from scratch for new system faults.

narrative_sequence.summary: RCA identifies root causes of system faults or failures from system monitoring data.
Efficient RCA can accelerate system failure recovery and mitigate system damage or financial losses.
Prior work has largely emphasized offline RCA, with manual initiation, costly training requirements, and full retraining for new faults.

source_observation.claim: Offline RCA can require manual initiation, substantial training time and data, and retraining from scratch for new system faults.

interpretation.claim: RCA systems may benefit from designs that support timely operation and adaptation to changing fault conditions.

application.claim: When designing monitoring-based diagnosis workflows, consider reducing manual triggering and avoiding full retraining after fault changes.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish that these design changes are effective in a particular system or setting.
